headline: This law changes the rare pediatric disease priority review voucher program, which lets drug makers speed up FDA review of certain drugs for serious childhood diseases.
what_it_does: The law amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to revise a program that gives a transferable voucher to drug sponsors who develop treatments for rare pediatric diseases. A voucher lets its holder have a new drug application reviewed by the FDA within six months. Sponsors must tell the FDA when they submit an application that they plan to request a voucher, starting 90 days after enactment. The law also limits eligibility, bars a second voucher for the same medication, and directs the Government Accountability Office to study whether the program works as intended.

who_it_affects.group: Drug companies developing treatments for rare pediatric diseases
who_it_affects.how: They must notify the FDA when submitting an application if they plan to request a priority review voucher, and applications filed before October 7, 2012 are not eligible.

who_it_affects.group: Families of children with rare serious diseases
who_it_affects.how: The program is limited to treatments for serious diseases, and it is set to end at the end of 2016 under the summary provided.
The agency must receive voucher notices from sponsors and cannot issue a voucher for a product that already received one under another program.

when_it_takes_effect: The notification requirement starts 90 days after enactment on September 30, 2016, and the bill applies to pending unapproved applications.
